title: Kubernetes Security & Observability Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on securing pods with securityContext and Pod Security Standards admission, then observing them with metrics-server, kubectl logs and events, and Prometheus basics.

chapters.title: Kubernetes Security & Observability Cover
points: securityContext
Pod Security Standards
Admission control
metrics-server and kubectl top
Logs and events
Prometheus basics

chapters.title: securityContext: Hardening a Pod
points: securityContext sets privilege and access controls; pod-level (spec.securityContext) applies to all containers, container-level overrides it
runAsNonRoot: true makes kubelet refuse to start a container whose image runs as UID 0; it checks, it does not change the user
runAsUser/runAsGroup/fsGroup set the UIDs; fsGroup changes group ownership of mounted volumes (pod-level only)
readOnlyRootFilesystem: true blocks writes to the container filesystem; mount an emptyDir at /tmp or other write paths the app needs
capabilities: drop: [ALL] then add only what is needed (e.g. NET_BIND_SERVICE); allowPrivilegeEscalation: false blocks setuid gains; privileged: true gives near-host access and should be avoided

chapters.title: Pod Security Standards and Admission
points: Three PSS levels: privileged (unrestricted), baseline (blocks known escalations like hostNetwork, privileged, hostPath), restricted (hardened: non-root, drop ALL, seccomp RuntimeDefault)
Pod Security Admission is the built-in controller that enforces PSS per namespace via labels, replacing removed PodSecurityPolicy
Namespace label pod-security.kubernetes.io/<mode>=<level> with modes enforce (reject), audit (log to audit log), warn (show user warning)
Roll out safely: set warn and audit to restricted first, fix violations, then set enforce; kubectl label ns dev pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted
PSA checks Pods only: workloads like Deployments are created but their Pods get rejected, so errors show in ReplicaSet events; for custom rules use Kyverno or Gatekeeper

chapters.title: metrics-server and kubectl top
points: metrics-server collects CPU and memory from each kubelet and serves them via the metrics.k8s.io API; it is in-memory, with no history
It powers kubectl top and the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler; it is not a monitoring system and does not store data
kubectl top nodes; kubectl top pods -A; kubectl top pod NAME --containers; add --sort-by=cpu
CPU is shown in millicores (250m = 0.25 core) and memory in Mi; values are a recent average, so brief spikes are missed
Error 'Metrics API not available' means metrics-server is missing or unhealthy; check its Deployment in kube-system (local clusters often need --kubelet-insecure-tls)

chapters.title: Logs and Events
points: kubectl logs POD reads container stdout/stderr from the node; flags: -c container, -f follow, --tail=100, --since=1h, -l app=web for a label selector
kubectl logs --previous shows the last crashed container's logs, the first step for CrashLoopBackOff
Logs vanish when the pod is deleted or the node rotates them; production needs a log collector (Fluent Bit, Loki) shipping to central storage
kubectl describe pod shows the Events section (scheduling, image pull, probe failures, OOMKilled); kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp -n NS lists them
Events expire after about 1 hour, so check them early; logs answer what the app said, events answer what Kubernetes did

chapters.title: Prometheus Basics and Cheat Sheet
points: Prometheus pulls (scrapes) metrics over HTTP from /metrics endpoints on a schedule and stores them as time series with labels
Metric types: counter (only increases, use rate()), gauge (up and down), histogram (buckets, use histogram_quantile)
Discovery: Kubernetes service discovery finds targets; the Operator uses ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor CRDs; the up metric is 1 when a target scrapes fine
PromQL: rate(http_requests_total[5m]); sum by (pod)(...); alerts via Alertmanager, dashboards in Grafana; Prometheus is for trends, metrics-server for kubectl top and HPA

Cheat sheet: securityContext = runAsNonRoot + readOnlyRootFilesystem + drop ALL; PSA = namespace label enforce/audit/warn; kubectl top = now; logs --previous = crash; events = k8s actions; Prometheus = history
